description: An independent community for NVIDIA Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal and GeForce GTX 16 (Turing) owners on Windows. Join GRELECY and help shape its goals.
hero_intro: An independent community exploring a longer useful life for NVIDIA Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal and GeForce GTX 16 (Turing) graphics hardware on Windows.
logo_alt: GRELECY emblem: a silver G on a green graphics card
stage_detail: No drivers or stable software; an experimental diagnostics tool is available.
project_intro: Working hardware can still have value after official support ends. GRELECY brings owners, testers and developers together to document problems and explore what is possible.
project_method: We start with evidence, share what we learn, and choose achievable goals together.
research_intro: Our first AI and gaming plan proposes reproducible experiments: local inference, compatibility and game profiles. The community will choose the next objective from the results.
roadmap_intro: Start with the available GTX 1060, with its variant and VRAM still to confirm. Extend testing as hardware and volunteers become available, within the Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal and GTX 16 Turing scope on Windows.
roadmap_status: Experiments not started. An illustrative 10–12 week cycle from an agreed kickoff, depending on available resources. M2 and M3 may overlap. GRELECY has not measured any gains yet; GitHub tickets hold current progress.
roadmap_m0_detail: Priority P0. Confirm the card, memory and environment; select models, audio and three game scenarios; freeze the comparison protocol before testing.
roadmap_m1_detail: Priority P0, after M0. Verify engine, CUDA and driver versions together, actual GPU execution and correct results, with an operational CPU fallback.
roadmap_m2_detail: Priority P0, after M0 and M1. Compare a small quantized language model and local audio transcription: speed, memory, quality and stability against CPU and GPU references.
roadmap_m3_detail: Priority P1, after M0. Compare three scenarios, VRAM profiles and upscalers available in each game, publishing FPS, frame times and visual tradeoffs.
roadmap_m4_title: Publish evidence and choose what follows
roadmap_m4_detail: Priority P1, after M2 and M3. Review results, seek independent reproduction, and document gains, failures and limits before recommending a configuration.
roadmap_lab_detail: Priority P2, without blocking software experiments. Assess nv-uefi-unlocker, whose GTX 16 hardware validation remains pending, separately from ReBAR, which concerns memory mapping and may require flashing the motherboard UEFI. These feasibility studies do not authorize a flash.
scope_note: Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal and Turing-based GTX 16 cards are in the initial community scope. Technical priorities will be chosen together. Exact GPU models matter. No support is guaranteed.
contribute_intro: You do not need to write code to contribute.
join_detail: Share your Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal or GeForce GTX 16 hardware, interests and skills.
report_detail: Record your GPU, Windows build and reproduction steps.
propose_detail: Bring a focused question and a way to test it.
independence: Independent community project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NVIDIA.
